messages.subject: awkward behaviour of ggplot legend
parts:

i found a kind of an akward behaviour in ggplot's legends. When comparing my two plots (code below), the order of the both legends is reversed (instrument top/bottom), although the only difference between both plots is that the text is shorter. Is there any way to fix the order of legends? Thanks in advance, Hans

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: awkward behaviour of ggplot legend
parts:
Hi Hans,

That is strange! I don't see why the length of the title should change
the order. Fortunately you can specify the order using guides(), e.g.,

ggplot(Depr_data, aes(x = est)) +
geom_density(aes(y=..density.. * 300, group = Depression, fill =
Depression), alpha = .3) +
scale_fill_grey("Distribution of theta", start=.6, end = .3) +

geom_line(aes(y = CI, linetype = instrument), size = .75) +
guides(fill=guide_legend(order=2), linetype=guide_legend(order=1))

Best,
Ista

On 1/3/2013 9:29 AM, Ista Zahn wrote:
> Hi Hans,
>
> That is strange! I don't see why the length of the title should change
> the order. Fortunately you can specify the order using guides(), e.g.,
>
> ggplot(Depr_data, aes(x = est)) +
> geom_density(aes(y=..density.. * 300, group = Depression, fill =
> Depression), alpha = .3) +
> scale_fill_grey("Distribution of theta", start=.6, end = .3) +
> geom_line(aes(y = CI, linetype = instrument), size = .75) +
> guides(fill=guide_legend(order=2), linetype=guide_legend(order=1))

If I recall, the order of the guides was deterministic, but dependent on
some hash of the whole legend (or something like that) that was
sensitive to any changes in the legend and could not be (easily)
predicted. The order parameter was included so that the order could be
set when that was a relevant consideration.

> Best,
> Ista
